Only the eight files in patch.diff differ from base (CHANGELOG.md, rich/_windows_renderer.py, rich/console.py, rich/control.py, rich/segment.py, tests/test_console.py, tests/test_control.py, tests/test_windows_renderer.py). generated/.git is harness state, not a patch change.

Reference-only test changes (tests/test_live.py, a new test_title name in the reference, and the reference's control.py __main__ demo) are absent from the candidate. Under the rules these are not deletions, and the candidate's own tests cover the same behaviour.
rich/segment.py:33 adds ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 to the existing ControlType enum, which is where the reference adds it (reference rich/segment.py:52).
rich/control.py:33 adds the format entry to CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT, and rich/control.py:144-153 adds Control.title beside show_cursor/alt_screen. The reference has the same placements.

rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56 unpacks `_, title = cast(Tuple[ControlType, str], control_code)` and calls `term.set_title(title)`. LegacyWindowsTerm.set_title(self, title: str) -> None exists at rich/_win32_console.py:534 inside class LegacyWindowsTerm (defined at line 306), so the call resolves.

rich/segment.py:36-41 extends ControlCode with Tuple[ControlType, str] as its own member. The reference widens to Tuple[ControlType, Union[int, str]]. Both are valid typings; the candidate's is more precise and keeps the existing members.

The candidate adds no import statements to rich/control.py, rich/segment.py, rich/console.py, or rich/_windows_renderer.py. The Windows renderer already imports LegacyWindowsTerm and ControlType/Segment, and it only calls methods on the term object it receives.

The candidate registers SET_WINDOW_TITLE in both dispatch sites: CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT at control.py:33 and the legacy Windows renderer at _windows_renderer.py:54.

The title is modeled as a Control payload (control.py:144) and rendered through the same two paths as every other control: the ANSI format map (control.py:33) for normal terminals, and the legacy renderer for Windows (_windows_renderer.py:54-56).

The reference puts the feature in the same modules, so the candidate's placement matches the intended architecture.

The candidate extends the existing ControlType enum, CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT map, ControlCode union, and legacy_windows_render if/elif chain (control.py:33, segment.py:33 and 36-41, _windows_renderer.py:54-56). No parallel path or new registry is introduced.

evidence: Behaviour matches the reference: Console.set_window_title writes the OSC 0 title control only when is_terminal is true and returns True (console.py:1164-1168). It returns False otherwise, matching the reference contract (reference rich/console.py:1205-1208).
Legacy Windows consoles receive the control through the renderer and call term.set_title (_windows_renderer.py:54-56), which is the required Windows path.

Control.title produces Segment text `\x1b]0;hello\x07` with control `[(ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE, "hello")]` (control.py:33, 153), which matches the reference's test expectation (reference tests/test_control.py:48-55).
No regressions: the new ControlCode member is additive, the existing formats are unchanged, and no existing dispatch branch is altered.

The candidate's console docstring omits some of the reference's long caveats about terminal support and title persistence. It keeps the essential note that terminals may reset or ignore the title, so the behavioural contract is intact.
